items.title: DSA kya hai aur interview mein kaise use hota hai
items.one_idea: DSA is two things, a data structure (how data is organised) and an algorithm (the steps that use it), and an interview checks whether your steps still work when the data is huge: 10 lakh sorted names take up to 1,000,000 checks one by one but about 20 with halving.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: 10 लाख names में एक name, 20 steps में कैसे ढूँढोगे?
items.hook_source: carried-over LearnAI hypothesis, first DSA test; hookscore 46.5 WEAK, no DEALBREAKER
items.visual_idea: A long row of name tiles with a magnifier moving one tile at a time and a step counter climbing toward 1,000,000, crossed out in red; then the same row halved again and again, the counter stopping at 20; chips DATA STRUCTURE (the row) and ALGORITHM (the halving moves) land on the objects when named.
items.everyday_anchor: Finding one contact among 10 lakh saved numbers: sorted list opened in the middle like a dictionary.
items.example: EXAMPLE (researcher ran it): 10 lakh sorted ints, target last: one-by-one 1000000 comparisons (worst case), halving 20. Printed: 1000000 20 True. Counts, not seconds.
facts_to_verify: Run both searches on 1,000,000 sorted ints and show real printed counts (1000000 and 20).
Amazon claim only: its page says learn how to approach data structures and algorithms in your interview; no claim about all companies, no claim about why.
The why-interviews-ask line is labelled as our own reasoning.
Halving needs a SORTED list; said on screen.

items.title: Big-O: steps ka growth, seconds nahi
items.one_idea: Big-O says how the number of steps grows when the input grows: one-by-one search grows in step with the data (10 lakh to 20 lakh names is 10 lakh to 20 lakh steps), halving adds one step, checking every pair quadruples when data doubles.
items.hook_source: owner-written script 2026-10-19; kept as written (lint hook check FAIL is a heuristic, owner wording wins)
items.hook_10s: 10{दस} लाख names search करने हैं। एक method को लगेंगे 10{दस} लाख steps, और दूसरे को सिर्फ़ 20{बीस}! Same problem, इतना बड़ा difference?

hook_candidates.hook: Data दोगुना करो, search में बस एक step बढ़ता है।
तुम्हारा code slow है, या तुम्हारा approach?
Interviewer ने पूछा: इस code की time complexity क्या है?

items.visual_idea: Two rows of name tiles side by side, then each row doubles in length: the one-by-one row's step counter doubles (10 lakh to 20 lakh) while the halving row's counter moves 20 to 21; a third row of pair-lines between every two tiles grows to four times as many lines when the row doubles; chips BIG-O, O(n), O(log n), O(n squared) land on the counters when named.
items.everyday_anchor: Finding one contact among your saved numbers: scrolling one by one gets twice as long when you save twice as many contacts, while opening the sorted list in the middle adds only one more look.
items.example: EXAMPLE (researcher ran it, counts not seconds): worst case, one-by-one search 1,000,000 and 2,000,000 steps for n = 10 lakh and 20 lakh; halving 20 and 21 steps (target last); pairs check 499,500 steps at n = 1,000 and 1,999,000 at n = 2,000 (about 4 times). 40 lakh names: halving 22.
facts_to_verify: Run all counts again and show the real printed output on screen (1000000 and 2000000 linear; 20 and 21 halving, target last; 499500 and 1999000 pairs).

Wikipedia Big O notation: growth rates as the variable becomes large; an upper bound on growth; constant factors and lower-order terms omitted. 'Steps, not seconds' is our own framing of growth of steps, not a quote; do not attribute it to the source.
Python wiki: x in list is O(n) average; x in set is O(1) average (worst case O(n)); never say always O(1).
Halving needs a SORTED list; say it on screen. It takes at most floor(log2 n)+1 steps; say 'about 20' or name the target-last case.
Seconds differ per machine (0.022 s was one run on a runner): do NOT put a time on screen as a fact.
items.script_notes: Numbers in Devanagari words (owner d001): 10{दस} लाख, 20{बीस}, 21{इक्कीस}. No 'wrong way first' announcement: the one-by-one search appears inside the story ('मान लो 10 लाख names हैं'). Nothing between hook and first teaching line (no rhetorical question). Terms: Big-O, O(n), O(log n); O(n squared) only in the catch beat. Header tag carries the day counter: DSA 002/150. Catch beat (about 75 percent): small inputs hide it (10 names: 45 vs 10 steps, both instant), Big-O is about growth when data gets big, constant factors dropped. OWNER WROTE THIS SCRIPT: keep wording; shorten only by deleting whole lines.
